categories.main_business_segments: D.R. Horton operates through four main business segments: homebuilding (core business), residential lot development (Forestar), financial services (mortgage and title), and rental operations (multi-family and single-family rentals). Homebuilding generates the vast majority of revenue, with Forestar supporting lot development, financial services providing mortgage and title services, and rental operations developing, leasing, and selling rental properties.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes a decentralized operating model for homebuilding, with local divisions responsible for site selection, land acquisition, construction management, and sales. Most land development and home construction is performed by subcontractors, selected through competitive bidding. D.R. Horton leverages economies of scale for purchasing materials and labor, and employs technology systems for operational, marketing, and financial management.
categories.primary_customers_markets: D.R. Horton primarily serves individual homebuyers across a broad spectrum, including entry-level, move-up, active adult, and luxury buyers. The company also sells homes to investors in the rental market and provides mortgage and title services mainly to its homebuyers. Its end markets are predominantly residential real estate buyers in the United States.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in 106 markets across 33 states, making it the most geographically diverse homebuilder in the U.S. Its homebuilding divisions are grouped into six reporting regions: Northwest, Southwest, South Central, Southeast, East, and North, covering major metropolitan and suburban areas nationwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: D.R. Horton is primarily a downstream operator, focusing on the development, construction, and sale of finished homes to end buyers. Through Forestar, it also has a significant presence in the upstream lot development segment, supplying finished lots to its own homebuilding operations and occasionally to third parties.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on maximizing returns on inventory investments, maintaining geographic and product diversification, and enhancing operational efficiency. Key initiatives include expanding relationships with land developers, increasing the use of lot purchase contracts, investing in rental property development, and continuous improvement in operational execution. ESG initiatives and home energy efficiency are also emerging areas of focus.
categories.revenue_model: D.R. Horton generates revenue primarily through the sale of completed homes, which accounted for 95% of consolidated revenues in 2022. Additional revenue streams include land and lot sales (mainly through Forestar), mortgage origination and title services, and the development, leasing, and sale of rental properties.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes with local, regional, and national homebuilders, as well as with existing home sales and rental properties. Major competitors include Lennar, PulteGroup, and other large public builders. D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the U.S. by volume and is a market leader in most of its operating regions, benefiting from its scale and geographic diversity.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2022, D.R. Horton reported $33.5 billion in consolidated revenues, closing 82,744 homes with an average price of $385,100. Net income attributable to D.R. Horton was $5.86 billion, with a return on equity of 34.5%. The company has demonstrated strong growth in revenue and profitability over recent years, supported by increased home sales and higher average selling prices.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: D.R. Horton emphasizes affordability, geographic reach, and product diversity, offering homes for a wide range of buyers from entry-level to luxury. Its scale enables cost efficiencies, competitive pricing, and reliable delivery. The company’s decentralized local management, strong balance sheet, and integrated financial services further differentiate its customer experience and operational resilience.
